item.title: MINISTER UMAHI VOWS TO RESIGN IF ABUJA-KADUNA-KANO ROAD PROJECT FAILS QUALITY TEST
item.description: While defending the 3.4 trillion naira budget proposal of the ministry, the minister argued that the current funding method is hindering the effective execution of projects under the ministry, adding that over 95 per cent of projects under the Federal Ministry of Works are ongoing, making consistent and adequate capital releases critical [...]

item.title: PRESIDENT TINUBU APPOINTS NEW NAHCON CHAIRMAN
item.description: The statement added that President TINUBU, has sent a letter to the Senate President, GODSWILL AKPABIO, requesting the expeditious confirmation of Ambassador Yusuf to replace Professor ABDULLAHI USMAN, who resigned this week, after about 14 months in the post.

item.title: SENATE DEFENDS DECISION ON E-TRANSMISSION OF ELECTION RESULTS,
item.description: The upper chamber said the decision was based on the stark realities of the country and not on emotions or sentiment after due consultation and engagement with principal actors in the country’s communications and power sectors, among others.

item.title: JOEBOY MAKES REMARKS ON AFROBEATS’ AUTHENTIC ROOTS.
item.description: Recall that at the beginning of the 2020s' decade, the Nigerian music industry saw a heavy fusion of Afrobeats with other genres, especially South Africa’s Amapiano, American hip-hop and R&B.

item.title: TOKE MAKINWA DEFENDS DECISION TO HIDE DAUGHTER’S FACE ONLINE
item.description: MAKINWA, who welcomed her daughter in 2025, has consistently posted photos and videos of the child, known as YAYA, while deliberately concealing her face.

item.title: MAN CITY BEAT ARSENAL 2–0 TO WIN CARABAO CUP AT WEMBLEY
item.description: Manager PEP GUARDIOLA saw his side bounce back strongly after their midweek UEFA Champions League exit at the hands of Real Madrid, which ended their hopes of a quadruple, while Arsenal, entered the match still competing on multiple fronts and aiming to keep their trophy ambitions alive.

item.title: IGP DISU DEBUNKS REPORT OF DISBANDING POLICE UNITS NATIONWIDE
item.description: In a statement issued by Force spokesperson ANTHONY PLACID, the police chief described the circulating claims as inaccurate and misleading, stressing that the directive in question does not involve scrapping units but rather streamlining the number of tactical teams to improve efficiency and oversight.

item.title: NIGERIA GOVERNORS’ FORUM SUBMITS STATE POLICE FRAMEWORK TO NATIONAL ASSEMBLY
item.description: The high-level meeting was attended by several state governors, including HOPE UZODINMA, ALEX OTTI, UMO ENO, DOUYE DIRI, HYACINTH ALIA, PETER MBAH among others.

item.title: SENATOR NATASHA BLAMES PDP CRISIS FOR DEFECTIONS, AND CALLS FOR RETURN.
item.description: AKPOTI-UDUAGHAN spoke of the weekend in Abuja during the inauguration of the PDP convention committee, an event viewed by party leaders as a vital move toward restoring unity and repositioning the opposition ahead of upcoming elections.

item.title: PORTABLE LINKS 2027 ELECTION TO SPIRITUAL JUDGMENT.
item.description: He referenced cultural and spiritual beliefs, suggesting that those who oppose president TINUBU may face consequences, and invoked spiritual entities as symbolic forces tied to justice and leadership.
